about.title: About Me
about.description: I am a final-year Engineering Science (Robotics) student at the University of Toronto working on embodied AI. My research asks how robots can learn from their own failures: coding agents that build and repair robot programs, harnesses that carry that experience across tasks, and benchmarks that show where VLA and world action models break. I am an undergraduate researcher in the Robot Vision and Learning Lab with Prof. Florian Shkurti and a research assistant at Huawei Noah's Ark Lab. Our team won 1st place in the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge at CoRL 2026. I am applying to master's and PhD programs for Fall 2027.

about.title: About Me
about.description: I am a final-year Engineering Science (Robotics) student at the University of Toronto working on embodied AI. My research asks how robots can learn from their own failures: coding agents that build and repair robot programs, harnesses that carry that experience across tasks, and benchmarks that show where VLA and world action models break. I am an undergraduate researcher in the Robot Vision and Learning Lab with Prof. Florian Shkurti and a research assistant at Huawei Noah's Ark Lab. Our team won 1st place in the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge at CoRL 2026. I am applying to master's and PhD programs for Fall 2027.

rvl.title: Undergraduate Researcher
rvl.company: UofT Robot Vision and Learning Lab (Prof. Florian Shkurti)
points: Designed an episodic memory module for frozen VLA policies (π0.5) that stores context, plan, failure, and recovery in one entry to support plan selection and failure recovery on memory-dependent manipulation tasks (RMBench); analyzed which failure modes cross-episode memory can and cannot fix.

Undergraduate thesis on agentic learning from failed attempts in code-as-policy robotics, where a frozen coding agent converts rollout videos, API traces, and scores into verified, failure-specific progress checks. Evaluating on RoboTwin 2.0 and EmbodiedSWE-Bench, with a 22-percentage-point improvement in task success on RoboTwin 2.0 so far.

huawei.title: Research Assistant
huawei.company: Huawei Technologies, Noah's Ark Lab - Embodied AI
points: Major contributor to The North Star's BEHAVIOR Challenge system: 1st place at CoRL 2026 (Q score 0.683; 48.2% full-task success on 100 household tasks), after 4th place at NeurIPS 2025. Built the agentic harness, whose capability- and history-based policy cards route tasks among VLA policies and a skill library of FSM pipelines combining SAM6D, π0.5, and TAMP. Built the HiPhys-RSI proof of concept, where a frozen-VLM coding agent composes tools into code pipelines and revises them from rollout videos and logs, and validated it for whole-body control and long-horizon manipulation.

Conducted large-scale robustness evaluations of VLAs (π0.5, X-VLA) and world action models (LingBot-VA, Fast-WAM, GE-Act, Cosmos-Policy) on LIBERO-Plus, and built RoboTwin 2.0-Plus, a dual-arm benchmark with the same perturbation protocol. Analyzed how vision, language, object layout, and robot initial-state perturbations affect each model family: WAMs are more robust to noise, lighting, and layout (74.2% vs. 58.6% for π0.5 on RoboTwin 2.0-Plus), while camera and initial-state shifts remain hard.

Led the design of two benchmarks for open problems in VLA and WAM evaluation, safe manipulation under clutter and anticipation of future dynamics: RoboPRO, 80 bimanual tasks with 16K demonstrations and safety-aware contact metrics; and RoboDyna, 30 dynamic tasks with synchronized and asynchronous evaluation protocols that isolate the effect of inference latency. Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 and RSS 2026 workshops.

Proposed the Agentic Adversarial Harness (A²H): a coding agent designs task variations that break its own robot programs, repairs them, and distills the failures into a reusable harness that transfers to unseen environments, raising real-robot first-attempt success from 15% to 60%. Co-developed RoboHarness, which orchestrates VLA, WAM, RL, and TAMP policies as agentic skills with memory-guided handoffs. A²H was accepted at CoRL 2026 (Late Breaking Results); RoboHarness received the Best Paper Award (oral) at the ECCV 2026 Workshop on Agent in World.

For the Self-CriTeach project, fine-tuned LLMs for long-horizon symbolic planning on self-generated PDDL domains with chain-of-thought self-teaching and self-critiquing constrained RL, and compared training recipes. Raised Qwen3-4B planning success from 26% to 46% (above GPT-4o at 19%); on a real UR5e robot it reached 70% vs. 40% for a PDDL solver. Accepted at ICML 2026.

crl.title: Undergraduate Research Assistant
crl.company: UofT Continuum Robotics Laboratory (Prof. Jessica Burgner-Kahrs)
points: Studied state estimation for tendon-driven continuum robots (TDCR), extending the Clarke transformation to general TDCR models to characterize actuation constraints and degrees of freedom.

Derived TDCR forward kinematics from first principles and built MuJoCo simulations; compared them with physical robots and introduced corrective factors for hardware effects such as material stiffness, disk radius, and tendon length. Documented results for the OpenCR project.

story.title: Background Story
story.content: Hoshipu is a little spirit from the stars who came to Earth out of curiosity about the human world. It loves observing human life and has developed a strong interest in programming and creation. Although sometimes lazy, once engaged in something interesting, it gives its all. Its name comes from the Japanese word 'hoshi' (star) and 'pu', symbolizing writing stories with starlight.
